title: Light-induced nonadiabatic dissipative quantum dynamics of the Na2 molecule
authors: Patrick Barron, Krisztián Szabó, Gábor J. Halász, Kálmán Varga, Ágnes Vibók
abstract: Strong light-matter coupling between molecules and optical or plasmonic cavity modes has emerged as a promising platform for advancing photonics, materials science, and chemistry. However, optical cavities and plasmonic resonators in particular are inherently lossy systems characterized by finite photon lifetimes. Accurate theoretical descriptions of molecular dynamics under strong coupling therefore require a proper treatment of cavity losses. In this work, we compare three theoretical approaches for modeling dissipative molecule-cavity dynamics within a realistic parameter regime: the Lindblad master equation, the stochastic Schrödinger equation, and the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation. As an example, we consider the two lowest energy state of Na2 molecule coupled to a cavity mode and analyze the time evolution of the excited-state population and the mean photon number. Our results demonstrate that the stochastic Schrödinger equation provides an accurate and computationally efficient alternative to the Lindblad master equation, while the non-Hermitian Schrödinger approach is found to be applicable only within a limited range of conditions. Furthermore, we show that inclusion of molecular rotation leads to rotational-vibrational-photonic coupling and gives rise to pronounced nonadiabatic dynamics through light-induced conical intersections. These findings highlight the importance of both dissipation and rotational degrees of freedom for a realistic description of molecular dynamics in strongly coupled molecule-cavity systems.
summary: The paper investigates how light drives a diatomic molecule coupled to a lossy optical cavity, focusing on the role of dissipation and molecular rotation. By comparing three major quantum simulation techniques (Lindblad ME, SE, TDSE), the authors establish the stochastic Schrödinger equation as the most reliable method for open dynamics. The key finding is that including rotational motion reveals nonadiabatic coupling pathways (LICIs) essential for accurate predictions.
main_problem: The study models the light-induced nonadiabatic dissipative quantum dynamics of a $	ext{Na}_2$ molecule coupled to a lossy optical or plasmonic cavity mode.
main_result: The stochastic Schrödinger equation is shown to be an accurate and efficient alternative to the Lindblad master equation for describing dissipation, while molecular rotation introduces crucial nonadiabatic coupling leading to light-induced conical intersections (LICIs).
method: The authors compare three theoretical frameworks—Lindblad Master Equation, Stochastic Schrödinger Equation, and Non-Hermitian Schrödinger Equation—to model open quantum dynamics.
model_or_system: The system involves the $	ext{Na}_2$ molecule coupled to a cavity mode, treated in an excited polaritonic manifold. The Hamiltonian includes terms for molecular vibration, rotation, and light-matter coupling, necessitating consideration of dissipation via cavity loss ($\gamma_c$).
key_observables: Excited-state population ($P_{	ext{ex}}(t)$) and mean photon number ($\langle N angle(t)$).
important_parameters: Cavity coupling strength ($g$), cavity loss rate ($\gamma_c$), laser pulse parameters (e.g., $E_{	ext{laser}}$, pulse length $T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares 1D models (fixed orientation) against full 2D models (including rotational dynamics); the Markovian Lindblad description is used for dissipation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate population and mean photon number dynamics comparing 1D vs. 2D treatments, showing how rotation induces nonadiabatic coupling (LICIs) and how different theoretical methods handle cavity loss.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares three computational techniques for open quantum systems: Lindblad ME, Stochastic SE, and Non-Hermitian TDSE. It progresses from simplified 1D models to full 2D treatments incorporating molecular rotation to reveal the necessity of considering both dissipation and angular degrees of freedom.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the complex intersection of cavity quantum electrodynamics (Cavity QED), nonadiabatic dynamics, and open system physics. The comparison of simulation methods provides crucial benchmarking for future theoretical modeling in molecular photonics.
